# ShieldCertificates — certifying primes, and why prime runs stop

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [Foundations: wheels, cycles and columns](../../GRAPH.md#foundations-wheels-cycles-and-columns)

If a set of wheels covers every prime up to the square root of the ceiling, surviving them proves primality, for single numbers, evenly spaced runs in either direction, and offset patterns. Conversely, a wheel that does not divide the spacing must block one of any run as long as the wheel itself, which caps the run length and forces the Lagrange–Waring condition on real prime runs. Between a cutoff and its square, prime means exactly "no wheel divides it." The certificates and windows rest on SquareRootShield; the Lagrange–Waring claims for real prime runs rest on Admissibility (a prime run's offset pattern is admissible); the other obstruction claims rest on no other node.

**What it adds:** Over Admissibility: the Lagrange–Waring condition there is about offset patterns; here it is forced on actual runs of primes, in both directions, and the square-root shield turns surviving the wheels into a primality certificate for each term of a run.

## Claims

<a id="prime_of_shield_cover"></a>
### `prime_of_shield_cover`

Surviving a set of wheels that covers the square root of the ceiling proves primality.

```lean
/-- **The shield certificate.** If a finite set of wheels contains every
prime whose square is at most the ceiling, then a number from 2 up to the
ceiling that no smaller wheel in the set divides is prime. -/
def prime_of_shield_cover : Prop :=
  ∀ (X n : Nat) (P : Finset Nat), 2 ≤ n → n ≤ X →
    (∀ q, q.Prime → q * q ≤ X → q ∈ P) → (∀ q ∈ P, q < n → ¬ q ∣ n) → n.Prime
```

**Rests on:** [`SquareRootShield.square_root_shield`](SquareRootShield.md#square_root_shield)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.prime_of_shield_cover_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="active_primes_cover"></a>
### `active_primes_cover`

Below the square of the bound, the active wheels cover every prime up to the square root.

```lean
/-- **The active wheels cover the ceiling.** When the ceiling is below the
square of the bound, every prime whose square is at most the ceiling is one
of the active wheels. -/
def active_primes_cover : Prop :=
  ∀ X L : Nat, X < L * L → ∀ q, q.Prime → q * q ≤ X → q ∈ active_primes L
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.active_primes_cover_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean)

<a id="family_prime_of_shield_cover"></a>
### `family_prime_of_shield_cover`

The shield certificate for any finite family of numbers.

```lean
/-- **The certificate for any finite family of numbers.** -/
def family_prime_of_shield_cover : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι : Type) (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → Nat) (X : Nat) (P : Finset Nat),
    (∀ q, q.Prime → q * q ≤ X → q ∈ P) → (∀ i ∈ s, 2 ≤ f i) → (∀ i ∈ s, f i ≤ X) →
    (∀ i ∈ s, ∀ q ∈ P, q < f i → ¬ q ∣ f i) → ∀ i ∈ s, (f i).Prime
```

**Rests on:** [`SquareRootShield.square_root_shield`](SquareRootShield.md#square_root_shield)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.family_prime_of_shield_cover_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="forward_ap_prime_of_active_shield"></a>
### `forward_ap_prime_of_active_shield`

Certifying an evenly spaced forward run.

```lean
/-- **Certifying a forward run** (a, a plus the spacing, …), given its last
term is within the ceiling. -/
def forward_ap_prime_of_active_shield : Prop :=
  ∀ a d k X L : Nat, X < L * L → a + (k - 1) * d ≤ X →
    (∀ i ∈ Finset.range k, 2 ≤ a + i * d) →
    (∀ i ∈ Finset.range k, ∀ q ∈ active_primes L, q < a + i * d → ¬ q ∣ a + i * d) →
    ∀ i ∈ Finset.range k, (a + i * d).Prime
```

**Rests on:** [`SquareRootShield.square_root_shield`](SquareRootShield.md#square_root_shield)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.forward_ap_prime_of_active_shield_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="backward_ap_prime_of_active_shield"></a>
### `backward_ap_prime_of_active_shield`

Certifying an evenly spaced backward run.

```lean
/-- **Certifying a backward run** (a, a minus the spacing, …), given its first
term is within the ceiling. -/
def backward_ap_prime_of_active_shield : Prop :=
  ∀ a d k X L : Nat, X < L * L → a ≤ X →
    (∀ i ∈ Finset.range k, 2 ≤ a - i * d) →
    (∀ i ∈ Finset.range k, ∀ q ∈ active_primes L, q < a - i * d → ¬ q ∣ a - i * d) →
    ∀ i ∈ Finset.range k, (a - i * d).Prime
```

**Rests on:** [`SquareRootShield.square_root_shield`](SquareRootShield.md#square_root_shield)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.backward_ap_prime_of_active_shield_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="tuple_prime_of_active_shield"></a>
### `tuple_prime_of_active_shield`

Certifying an offset pattern.

```lean
/-- **Certifying an offset pattern** (a starting number plus each offset). -/
def tuple_prime_of_active_shield : Prop :=
  ∀ (n X L : Nat) (T : Finset Nat), X < L * L →
    (∀ t ∈ T, 2 ≤ n + t) → (∀ t ∈ T, n + t ≤ X) →
    (∀ t ∈ T, ∀ q ∈ active_primes L, q < n + t → ¬ q ∣ n + t) →
    ∀ t ∈ T, (n + t).Prime
```

**Rests on:** [`SquareRootShield.square_root_shield`](SquareRootShield.md#square_root_shield)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.tuple_prime_of_active_shield_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="ap_hits_wheel"></a>
### `ap_hits_wheel`

A prime wheel not dividing the spacing divides a term of any run as long as the wheel.

```lean
/-- **The wheel obstruction.** A prime wheel that does not divide the spacing
divides some term among any run at least as long as the wheel. -/
def ap_hits_wheel : Prop :=
  ∀ a d k q : Nat, q.Prime → ¬ q ∣ d → q ≤ k → ∃ i ∈ Finset.range k, q ∣ a + i * d
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.ap_hits_wheel_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean)

<a id="ap_prime_run_length_lt_of_lt_start"></a>
### `ap_prime_run_length_lt_of_lt_start`

An all-prime run starting above such a wheel is shorter than the wheel.

```lean
/-- **Run-length bound.** An all-prime forward run starting above a prime
wheel that does not divide the spacing is shorter than that wheel. -/
def ap_prime_run_length_lt_of_lt_start : Prop :=
  ∀ a d k q : Nat, q.Prime → ¬ q ∣ d → q < a →
    (∀ i ∈ Finset.range k, (a + i * d).Prime) → k < q
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.ap_prime_run_length_lt_of_lt_start_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean)

<a id="ap_prime_run_forces_divisibility"></a>
### `ap_prime_run_forces_divisibility`

An all-prime run starting above its length has every prime up to its length dividing the spacing.

```lean
/-- **Lagrange–Waring, for actual prime runs.** If an all-prime forward run
starts above its own length, every prime up to that length divides the
spacing. -/
def ap_prime_run_forces_divisibility : Prop :=
  ∀ a d k : Nat, k < a → (∀ i ∈ Finset.range k, (a + i * d).Prime) →
    ∀ p, p.Prime → p ≤ k → p ∣ d
```

**Rests on:** [`Admissibility.ap_offsets_admissible_iff`](Admissibility.md#ap_offsets_admissible_iff)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.ap_prime_run_forces_divisibility_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="window_prime_iff"></a>
### `window_prime_iff`

From a cutoff to just below its square, prime means no wheel below the cutoff divides it.

```lean
/-- **The two-way window.** From the cutoff up to just below its square, a
number is prime exactly when no prime below the cutoff divides it. -/
def window_prime_iff : Prop :=
  ∀ cutoff n : Nat, cutoff ≤ n → n < cutoff * cutoff →
    (n.Prime ↔ ∀ q ∈ active_primes cutoff, ¬ q ∣ n)
```

**Rests on:** [`SquareRootShield.square_root_shield`](SquareRootShield.md#square_root_shield)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.window_prime_iff_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="window_twin_iff"></a>
### `window_twin_iff`

The two-way window for twin pairs.

```lean
/-- **The two-way window for twin pairs.** -/
def window_twin_iff : Prop :=
  ∀ cutoff n : Nat, cutoff ≤ n → n + 2 < cutoff * cutoff →
    ((n.Prime ∧ (n + 2).Prime) ↔
      ((∀ q ∈ active_primes cutoff, ¬ q ∣ n) ∧ (∀ q ∈ active_primes cutoff, ¬ q ∣ n + 2)))
```

**Rests on:** [`SquareRootShield.square_root_shield`](SquareRootShield.md#square_root_shield)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.window_twin_iff_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="backward_ap_hits_wheel"></a>
### `backward_ap_hits_wheel`

The wheel obstruction for backward runs.

```lean
/-- **The wheel obstruction, backward.** -/
def backward_ap_hits_wheel : Prop :=
  ∀ top step count q : Nat, q.Prime → ¬ q ∣ step → q ≤ count →
    (count - 1) * step ≤ top → ∃ i ∈ Finset.range count, q ∣ top - i * step
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.ShieldCertificates.backward_ap_hits_wheel_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ShieldCertificates.lean)

```lean
def backward_ap_prime_run_length_lt_of_above : Prop :=
  ∀ top step count q : Nat, q.Prime → ¬ q ∣ step → q < top - (count - 1) * step →
    (∀ i ∈ Finset.range count, (top - i * step).Prime) → count < q
```

<a id="backward_ap_prime_run_forces_divisibility"></a>
### `backward_ap_prime_run_forces_divisibility`

The Lagrange-Waring condition for backward runs.

```lean
/-- **Lagrange–Waring, backward.** -/
def backward_ap_prime_run_forces_divisibility : Prop :=
  ∀ top step count : Nat, count < top - (count - 1) * step →
    (∀ i ∈ Finset.range count, (top - i * step).Prime) →
    ∀ p, p.Prime → p ≤ count → p ∣ step
```

**Rests on:** [`Admissibility.ap_offsets_admissible_iff`](Admissibility.md#ap_offsets_admissible_iff)
